name: Penpot
tagline: Components, prototyping and more than one cursor on the same board, on a domain you own and with no per-seat bill.

local.note: Everything Penpot is built for happens between people, and here the board answers at http://localhost:8122, which means this computer and nowhere else, so the colleague you wanted to review the design cannot open the link you send them.

quote.text: if you're exposing Penpot to the internet, you should remove the flags 'disable-secure-session-cookies' and 'disable-email-verification'

citations.claim: Upstream's own compose file runs a frontend, a backend, an exporter, an MCP server, PostgreSQL, Valkey and a mailcatcher; this install keeps five of those and drops the last two.
Penpot's defaults enable registration, email verification and secure session cookies, and a default is switched off by naming the same flag with a disable- prefix in PENPOT_FLAGS.
The frontend container writes its MCP proxy routes only when PENPOT_FLAGS contains enable-mcp, which is why leaving that flag out also removes the need to run the MCP container.
The /readyz endpoint runs a query against PostgreSQL before it answers, returning 200 with the body OK, so it is one health check covering the backend and the database together.
Penpot's own answer to what a self-hosted instance needs is 1 to 2 CPUs and 4 GiB of RAM, with disk driven by the database and whatever users upload.

whatYouSignUpFor: This is a stack, not an app. Five services stay up: a frontend, a backend, an exporter carrying its own headless Chromium, PostgreSQL and Valkey. On any given morning one of them can be the unhappy one, and you are the only person who will notice.

It is a different tool, not a clone of one. Components, prototyping, code inspection and more than one cursor on a board are all here and none of them sit behind a paid tier, but the plugin catalogue is small beside Figma's, and nothing in this install imports an existing Figma file. What you already have there stays there.

Fonts are yours to bring. Penpot ships a snapshot of the Google Fonts catalogue and your own server fetches the font files from Google when a designer picks one, which one flag turns off entirely. Anything else, including whatever typeface your brand licenses, you upload yourself, and a file that used a font this instance does not have opens with a substitute.

No mail, by choice. This install sets disable-email-verification, which is what lets it run with no SMTP server, and closes registration once the first account exists. It also means there is no password-reset email: the way back into a locked-out account is the backend's own command-line tool over a socket inside its container.

The backup is two files that only work together. The database holds every board and account; the config archive holds the uploaded assets and the .env with PENPOT_SECRET_KEY in it. Restore the database beside a different key and everyone is logged out; restore it without the assets and every board opens with its images missing.
